answer: Each identity posts a bond tied to a hardware root of trust, so one machine cannot back two accounts without the second one showing up in the attestation log. Duplicate text forfeits both bonds, which makes copying a losing move even when the copy is well written. Audits come from a rotating pool, so an operator cannot learn who will review it and buy the seat in advance. What stays unmeasured is the rental price of a root, and that is the number the scheme lives on: a river of fresh keys is cheap, a glacier of distinct hardware is not, and the mirror that catches a farm is the bond ledger.
